targets.title: The Ideological Congruence Controversy: The Impact of Alternative Measures, Data, and Time Periods on the Effects of Election Rules
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for replication from Powell (2009) is that government congruence under SMD [single member district] is usually determined by the distance between the median voter and the plurality vote winner (Hypothesis 2a).
targets.outcome_quote:
In the original paper the estimate is positive (0.84) and significant. In the replication, the estimated coefficient was positive (0.9) and significant (p=0.000).

Thus the replication claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: In the original paper the estimate is positive (0.84) and significant. In the reproduction, the estimated coefficient was positive (0.84) and significant (p=0.000).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: There are no deviations for the reproduction data
targets.outcome_reasoning: The extended dataset replication meets the authors’ explicit success criterion. The report also includes a separate same-data reproduction, recovering the original focal coefficient 0.84; its computation is reproducible and no alternative original-data specifications are reported. Both components concern the same original paper, so only one target is listed.
